-- Cat Act 2011 (WA), Part 2 Division 1 -- registration and tagging.
-- Who must register a cat, when the duty does not apply, the tag duty and its
-- defence, and the closed list on which a local government must refuse an
-- application.
--
-- No library imports: see the note at the head of cat-domain.l4.
--
-- SCOPE. ss 14(2) and 18(2) are enacted in Divisions 2 and 3, so s 9(3) and
-- s 9(4) read them as facts supplied rather than by calling into the module
-- that encodes them. That is the scope discipline in CLAUDE.md, and it is why
-- the s 9 decisions take two extra booleans.

§ `Part 2 -- Registration, identification and sterilisation of cats`

§§ `Division 1 -- Registration and tagging`

§§§ `5 -- Cats to be registered`

-- The age condition, which ss 5(1), 14(1) and 18(1) share word for word:
-- "a cat that has reached 6 months of age".
GIVEN cat IS A Cat
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the cat has reached 6 months of age` IF
    cat's `age in months` AT LEAST 6

-- s 5(2): "Subsection (1) does not apply if -- (a) the cat has been kept by the
-- person for less than 14 days; or (b) the person has been resident in the
-- State for less than 14 days; or (c) the cat belongs to a class of cats
-- prescribed as exempt from registration."
--
-- NOTE ON "the person". s 5(1) imposes the duty on "the owner of a cat"; s 5(2)
-- paragraphs (a) and (b) then speak of "the person", a term s 5 never
-- introduces. Read as the owner, which is the only candidate antecedent in the
-- section and the reading encoded here. Recorded as an incident because the
-- defined term `owner` in s 4 can attach to more than one person at once --
-- s 4(1)(b) reaches "a person who, or an owner of a business or organisation
-- that, ordinarily keeps and cares for the cat" -- so which person's 14 days
-- are counted is not idle.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `section 5(2) disapplies the duty to register` IF
        "(a) the cat has been kept by the person for less than 14 days"
            ... `the situation`'s `days the cat has been kept by the owner` LESS THAN 14
    ..  "(b) the person has been resident in the State for less than 14 days"
            ... `the situation`'s `days the owner has been resident in the State` LESS THAN 14
    OR  "(c) the cat belongs to a class of cats prescribed as exempt from registration"
            ... `the situation`'s `of a class prescribed as exempt from registration`

-- s 5(1): "The owner of a cat that has reached 6 months of age must ensure that
-- the cat is registered with the local government in whose district the cat is
-- ordinarily kept."
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner must ensure the cat is registered` IF
        `the cat has reached 6 months of age` (`the situation`'s `cat`)
    AND NOT `section 5(2) disapplies the duty to register` `the situation`

-- The duty is to register WITH THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT IN WHOSE DISTRICT the cat
-- is ordinarily kept, so registration with some other local government does not
-- discharge it. `registered` alone is not enough, and that is why the `the situation`
-- carries both facts.
-- Breach is not the mere absence of registration: the Interpretation Act 1984
-- (WA) s 63 supplies the time the section leaves open, so an owner still
-- proceeding with all convenient speed is not yet in contravention. See FORK-2.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner contravenes section 5(1)` IF
        `the owner must ensure the cat is registered` `the situation`
    AND NOT `the situation`'s `the cat is registered with that local government`
    AND NOT "Interpretation Act 1984 s 63: with all convenient speed"
            ... `the situation`'s `the owner has proceeded with all convenient speed`

§§§ `6 -- Cats to wear tags`

-- s 6(3): the defence. Facts local to this section, so declared here rather
-- than in the shared ontology.
DECLARE Section6Defence HAS
    -- (a)(i)-(iii), three alternative causes.
    `the act or default of another person`   IS A BOOLEAN
    `an accident`                            IS A BOOLEAN
    `some other cause beyond the accused's control` IS A BOOLEAN
    -- (b), a conjunct in its own right: both limbs must hold.
    `the accused took reasonable precautions` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the accused could not by the exercise of due diligence have prevented the offence` IS A BOOLEAN

-- s 6(1): "The owner of a registered cat must ensure that when the cat is in a
-- public place the cat is wearing its registration tag."
--
-- The duty is conditional on the cat being IN A PUBLIC PLACE, and it attaches
-- only to the owner of a REGISTERED cat -- so an unregistered cat, whose owner
-- may be contravening s 5(1), cannot contravene s 6(1) at all.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner must ensure the cat is wearing its registration tag` IF
        "The owner of a registered cat" ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `registered`
    AND "when the cat is in a public place" ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `in a public place`
    AND NOT "(2) ... prescribed as exempt from wearing registration tags when in a public place"
            ... `the situation`'s `of a class prescribed as exempt from wearing a tag in a public place`

GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner contravenes section 6(1)` IF
        `the owner must ensure the cat is wearing its registration tag` `the situation`
    AND NOT `the situation`'s `cat`'s `wearing its registration tag`

-- s 6(3): "It is a defence to a charge under subsection (1) if the accused
-- establishes that -- (a) the contravention ... was due to -- (i) the act or
-- default of another person; or (ii) an accident; or (iii) some other cause
-- beyond the accused's control; and (b) the accused took reasonable precautions
-- and could not by the exercise of due diligence have prevented the commission
-- of the offence."
--
-- (a) is a disjunction of three, (b) is a conjunction of two, and the two
-- limbs are joined by AND. The burden is on the accused ("establishes"), which
-- the encoding cannot express and does not pretend to: this decides whether the
-- facts amount to the defence, not who must prove them.
GIVEN `the defence` IS A Section6Defence
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `paragraph (a) of section 6(3) is made out` IF
        "(a)(i) the act or default of another person"
            ... `the defence`'s `the act or default of another person`
    ..  "(a)(ii) an accident"
            ... `the defence`'s `an accident`
    OR  "(a)(iii) some other cause beyond the accused's control"
            ... `the defence`'s `some other cause beyond the accused's control`

GIVEN `the defence` IS A Section6Defence
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `paragraph (b) of section 6(3) is made out` IF
        "(b) the accused took reasonable precautions"
            ... `the defence`'s `the accused took reasonable precautions`
    AND "(b) and could not by the exercise of due diligence have prevented the commission of the offence"
            ... `the defence`'s `the accused could not by the exercise of due diligence have prevented the offence`

-- The two paragraphs are joined by "and", so both must be made out. Named
-- separately rather than nested, so that no line carries AND and OR at once.
GIVEN `the defence` IS A Section6Defence
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the section 6(3) defence is established` IF
        `paragraph (a) of section 6(3) is made out` `the defence`
    AND `paragraph (b) of section 6(3) is made out` `the defence`

§§§ `7 -- Interference with tag`

-- s 7: "A person must not, without reasonable excuse, remove or interfere with
-- a registration tag worn by a cat."
--
-- Two ways to offend and one excuse. `worn by a cat` is a condition on the tag:
-- a tag not being worn is outside the section.
DECLARE Section7Conduct HAS
    `the tag was worn by a cat`  IS A BOOLEAN
    `removed the tag`            IS A BOOLEAN
    `interfered with the tag`    IS A BOOLEAN
    `the person had a reasonable excuse` IS A BOOLEAN

GIVEN `the conduct` IS A Section7Conduct
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the person contravenes section 7` IF
        "a registration tag worn by a cat" ... `the conduct`'s `the tag was worn by a cat`
    AND (   "remove" ... `the conduct`'s `removed the tag`
         OR "interfere with" ... `the conduct`'s `interfered with the tag`)
    AND NOT "without reasonable excuse" ... `the conduct`'s `the person had a reasonable excuse`

§§§ `9 -- Registration`

-- s 9(2): "A local government must refuse an application for the grant or
-- renewal of the registration of a cat if, and only if, the local government is
-- satisfied that one or more of the following apply".
--
-- The list is closed, and "if, and only if" makes it exhaustive in both
-- directions: satisfied of one, refusal is mandatory; satisfied of none,
-- refusal is forbidden.
--
-- (c) and (d) are written here as the subsection reads them TOGETHER WITH
-- ss 9(3) and 9(4), which forbid refusal on those grounds where the cat is
-- exempt. Encoding (c) bare and then subtracting would produce a rule that says
-- refusal is mandatory and forbidden at once on the same facts.
-- (c) and (d) each carry their own carve-out, so each is a named rung. Writing
-- them inline would put AND and OR on the same chain, which the linter flags and
-- which hides the fact that (c) is itself a conjunction.
GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application,
      `the cat is exempt from microchipping as referred to in section 14(2)` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `ground (c) of section 9(2) applies` IF
        "(c) the cat is not microchipped"
            ... NOT `the application`'s `situation`'s `cat`'s `microchipped`
    AND "(3) ... must not refuse ... if the cat is exempt from microchipping as referred to in section 14(2)"
            ... NOT `the cat is exempt from microchipping as referred to in section 14(2)`

GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application,
      `the cat is exempt from sterilisation as referred to in section 18(2)` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `ground (d) of section 9(2) applies` IF
        "(d) the cat is not sterilised"
            ... NOT `the application`'s `situation`'s `cat`'s `sterilised`
    AND "(4) ... must not refuse ... if the cat is exempt from sterilisation as referred to in section 18(2)"
            ... NOT `the cat is exempt from sterilisation as referred to in section 18(2)`

GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application,
      `the cat is exempt from microchipping as referred to in section 14(2)` IS A BOOLEAN,
      `the cat is exempt from sterilisation as referred to in section 18(2)` IS A BOOLEAN
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `a ground in section 9(2) applies` IF
        "(a) the applicant is a child under 18 years of age"
            ... `the applicant is a child under 18 years of age` `the application`
    ..  "(b) the cat belongs to a class of cats prescribed as exempt from registration"
            ... `the application`'s `situation`'s `of a class prescribed as exempt from registration`
    ..  `ground (c) of section 9(2) applies` `the application`
            `the cat is exempt from microchipping as referred to in section 14(2)`
    ..  `ground (d) of section 9(2) applies` `the application`
            `the cat is exempt from sterilisation as referred to in section 18(2)`
    OR  "(e) convicted within the previous 3 years of 2 or more offences"
            ... `the application`'s `convictions in the previous 3 years for offences against this Act, the Dog Act 1976 or the Animal Welfare Act 2002` AT LEAST 2

GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the applicant is a child under 18 years of age` IF
    CONSIDER `the application`'s `applicant`'s `age`
    WHEN `a child under 18 years of age` THEN TRUE
    OTHERWISE FALSE

-- s 9(6): "The local government may refuse to consider an application if the
-- applicant does not comply with a requirement under subsection (5) within the
-- specified time." A power, not a duty, and it is a refusal to CONSIDER --
-- which is not one of the outcomes s 9(1) offers. See the incident register.
GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the local government may refuse to consider the application` IF
        "a requirement under subsection (5)" ... `the application`'s `a requirement under section 9(5) was made`
    AND NOT "within the specified time" ... `the application`'s `the applicant complied within the specified time`

-- s 9(5): the time specified must be "not more than 21 days". A requirement
-- that specifies longer is outside the power the subsection confers.
GIVEN `the application` IS AN Application
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the requirement under section 9(5) is within power` IF
    CONSIDER `the application`'s `the specified time in days`
    WHEN NOTHING THEN NOT `the application`'s `a requirement under section 9(5) was made`
    WHEN JUST days THEN days AT MOST 21

-- Cat Act 2011 (WA), Part 2 Divisions 2 and 3 -- microchipping and sterilisation.
-- The two duties that attach at 6 months, the certificates that excuse them,
-- and the notices a microchip implanter and a veterinarian must give.
--
-- No library imports: see the note at the head of cat-domain.l4.
--
-- The two Divisions are encoded in one module because they are the same shape
-- twice over -- duty at 6 months, exemption by veterinary certificate,
-- certificate unavailable below 6 months, 7-day notice to the microchip
-- database company -- and because two of the incidents this subject records are
-- about the difference between them.

§ `Part 2 -- Registration, identification and sterilisation of cats`

§§ `Division 2 -- Microchipping`

§§§ `14 -- Cats to be microchipped`

-- s 14(3): "A certificate referred to in subsection (2) cannot apply in respect
-- of a cat that is under 6 months of age." s 18(3) says the same of a
-- sterilisation certificate. So a certificate is spent unless the cat had
-- reached 6 months when it was given.
--
-- Written once and used by both Divisions: the subsections are word for word
-- the same test, and a reader checking either against this rule reads the same
-- sentence.
GIVEN `the certificate` IS A VetCertificate
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the certificate can apply to the cat` IF
        "given by a veterinarian" ... `the certificate`'s `given by a veterinarian`
    AND "applies in respect of the cat" ... `the certificate`'s `it applies in respect of the cat`
    AND "cannot apply in respect of a cat that is under 6 months of age"
            ... `the certificate`'s `the age in months of the cat when it was given` AT LEAST 6

-- s 14(2): "A cat is exempt from microchipping if a certificate given by a
-- veterinarian stating that the implantation of a microchip in the cat may
-- adversely affect the health and welfare of the cat applies in respect of the
-- cat."
--
-- The certificate is MAYBE: most cats have none, and the absence is the
-- ordinary case rather than a named outcome.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the cat is exempt from microchipping` IF
    CONSIDER `the situation`'s `certificate about microchipping`
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST c THEN `the certificate can apply to the cat` c

-- s 14(1): "The owner of a cat that has reached 6 months of age must ensure
-- that the cat is microchipped, unless the cat is exempt from microchipping."
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner must ensure the cat is microchipped` IF
        "a cat that has reached 6 months of age"
            ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `age in months` AT LEAST 6
    AND "unless the cat is exempt from microchipping"
            ... NOT `the cat is exempt from microchipping` `the situation`

-- As with s 5(1): the section fixes no time, so Interpretation Act 1984 (WA)
-- s 63 supplies one, and an owner proceeding with all convenient speed is not
-- yet in contravention. See FORK-2 in the fork register.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner contravenes section 14(1)` IF
        `the owner must ensure the cat is microchipped` `the situation`
    AND NOT `the situation`'s `cat`'s `microchipped`
    AND NOT "Interpretation Act 1984 s 63: with all convenient speed"
            ... `the situation`'s `the owner has proceeded with all convenient speed`

§§§ `15, 20 -- The notices owed to the microchip database company`

-- s 15: "A microchip implanter who implants a microchip in a cat must, within 7
-- days after the microchip is implanted, give notice in writing in the form, if
-- any, prescribed of the information prescribed to the microchip database
-- company for that cat."
--
-- s 20: "A veterinarian who sterilises a microchipped cat must, within 7 days
-- after sterilising the cat, give notice in writing ... of the sterilisation of
-- the cat to the microchip database company for that cat."
--
-- Both are duties on a named actor with a deadline, so both are regulative
-- rules. The deadline is 7 days from the triggering act, and the count is in
-- days because the Act counts in days.
DECLARE `A person who owes a notice` IS ONE OF
    `the microchip implanter`        -- s 15
    `the veterinarian who sterilised the cat`  -- s 20
    `the microchip database company`           -- s 16

DECLARE `An act under Division 2 or 3` IS ONE OF
    `give the prescribed information to the microchip database company`     -- s 15
    `give notice of the sterilisation to the microchip database company`    -- s 20
    `keep and maintain the prescribed information in the microchip database` -- s 16

-- s 15. LEST BREACH carries its reason, because the reason is what a trace
-- prints back and what a reader of the trace has to act on.
GIVETH A DEONTIC `A person who owes a notice` `An act under Division 2 or 3`
DECIDE `the duty under section 15` IS
    PARTY `the microchip implanter`
    MUST  `give the prescribed information to the microchip database company`
    WITHIN 7
    HENCE FULFILLED
    LEST  BREACH BY `the microchip implanter`
          BECAUSE "section 15: a microchip implanter who implants a microchip in a cat must give the prescribed information to the microchip database company within 7 days after the microchip is implanted"

-- s 20. Note the condition the section carries and this rule cannot: the duty
-- bites only where the cat sterilised was ALREADY MICROCHIPPED, because a cat
-- with no microchip has no microchip database company. Whether this cat was
-- microchipped is a fact of the situation, so the caller tests it before
-- reaching this obligation; see `the veterinarian owes the section 20 notice`.
GIVETH A DEONTIC `A person who owes a notice` `An act under Division 2 or 3`
DECIDE `the duty under section 20` IS
    PARTY `the veterinarian who sterilised the cat`
    MUST  `give notice of the sterilisation to the microchip database company`
    WITHIN 7
    HENCE FULFILLED
    LEST  BREACH BY `the veterinarian who sterilised the cat`
          BECAUSE "section 20: a veterinarian who sterilises a microchipped cat must give notice of the sterilisation to the microchip database company within 7 days after sterilising the cat"

-- s 20's gate: "A veterinarian who sterilises a MICROCHIPPED cat". A cat
-- sterilised before it was ever microchipped generates no notice under s 20,
-- and nothing else in Division 2 or 3 requires the sterilisation to be recorded
-- later. See the incident register.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the veterinarian owes the section 20 notice` IF
        "who sterilises" ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `sterilised by a veterinarian`
    AND "a microchipped cat" ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `microchipped`

§§ `Division 3 -- Sterilisation`

§§§ `18 -- Cats to be sterilised`

-- s 18(2): "A cat is exempt from sterilisation if any of the following apply in
-- respect of the cat -- (a) a certificate given by a veterinarian stating that
-- to sterilise the cat may adversely affect the health and welfare of the cat
-- applies in respect of the cat; (b) the cat is owned, for the purpose of
-- breeding, by an approved cat breeder; (c) the cat belongs to a class of cats
-- prescribed as exempt from sterilisation."
--
-- (b) is two conditions, not one: the owner must be an approved cat breeder AND
-- the cat must be owned for the purpose of breeding.
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `paragraph (b) of section 18(2) applies` IF
        "by an approved cat breeder" ... `the situation`'s `owner`'s `an approved cat breeder`
    AND "owned, for the purpose of breeding" ... `the situation`'s `owned for the purpose of breeding`

GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the certificate about sterilisation can apply` IF
    CONSIDER `the situation`'s `certificate about sterilisation`
    WHEN NOTHING THEN FALSE
    WHEN JUST c THEN `the certificate can apply to the cat` c

GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the cat is exempt from sterilisation` IF
        "(a) a certificate given by a veterinarian ... applies in respect of the cat"
            ... `the certificate about sterilisation can apply` `the situation`
    ..  "(b) the cat is owned, for the purpose of breeding, by an approved cat breeder"
            ... `paragraph (b) of section 18(2) applies` `the situation`
    OR  "(c) the cat belongs to a class of cats prescribed as exempt from sterilisation"
            ... `the situation`'s `of a class prescribed as exempt from sterilisation`

-- s 18(1): "The owner of a cat that has reached 6 months of age must ensure
-- that the cat is sterilised by a veterinarian, unless the cat is exempt from
-- sterilisation."
--
-- "by a veterinarian" is part of the duty, and it is NOT part of the s 3(1)
-- definition of `sterilised` ("made permanently infertile by a surgical
-- procedure"). So the duty and the definition can come apart, which is what the
-- incident register records: a cat sterilised otherwise than by a veterinarian
-- is `sterilised` for every other purpose in the Act while its owner remains in
-- breach of s 18(1).
GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner must ensure the cat is sterilised by a veterinarian` IF
        "a cat that has reached 6 months of age"
            ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `age in months` AT LEAST 6
    AND "unless the cat is exempt from sterilisation"
            ... NOT `the cat is exempt from sterilisation` `the situation`

GIVEN `the situation` IS A Situation
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the owner contravenes section 18(1)` IF
        `the owner must ensure the cat is sterilised by a veterinarian` `the situation`
    AND NOT "sterilised by a veterinarian" ... `the situation`'s `cat`'s `sterilised by a veterinarian`
    AND NOT "Interpretation Act 1984 s 63: with all convenient speed"
            ... `the situation`'s `the owner has proceeded with all convenient speed`

§§§ `19 -- Identifying as sterilised a cat that is not sterilised`

-- s 19: "A person must not identify a cat as sterilised in the manner
-- prescribed if it is not sterilised." The prescribed manner is a fact
-- supplied: the regulations were not retrieved.
DECLARE Section19Conduct HAS
    `identified the cat as sterilised in the manner prescribed` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the cat is sterilised`  IS A BOOLEAN

GIVEN `the conduct` IS A Section19Conduct
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the person contravenes section 19` IF
        "identify a cat as sterilised in the manner prescribed"
            ... `the conduct`'s `identified the cat as sterilised in the manner prescribed`
    AND "if it is not sterilised" ... NOT `the conduct`'s `the cat is sterilised`

-- Cat Regulations 2012 (WA) -- the prescribing regulations the Act leaves its
-- exemptions to, and the registration periods.
--
-- Source: sources/cat-regulations-2012.txt, converted from the register's own
-- mrdoc_48735.docx (sha256 ae3baa53a091d8f9...; the full digest is in
-- registers/source-bundle.json). Gazetted 16 Nov 2012 p. 5537-69.
--
-- WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS. cat-part2-div1-registration.l4 takes
-- `of a class prescribed as exempt from registration` and
-- `of a class prescribed as exempt from wearing a tag in a public place` as
-- facts supplied, because s 5(2)(c) and s 6(2) delegate them and the Act cannot
-- make them true. Regulations 9 and 10 are what makes them true. This module
-- decides them from facts about the cat's custody or its appearance at a show,
-- so that nothing about the exemptions rests on an unexplained boolean.
--
-- The Act module still takes them as inputs. That is the scope discipline in
-- CLAUDE.md and it is deliberate: the Act and the regulations are different
-- instruments, each amendable without the other, and a module that reached
-- across would hide which instrument a conclusion came from. The wiring is done
-- at the call site, in cat-cases.l4.
--
-- No library imports: see the note at the head of cat-domain.l4.

§ `Cat Regulations 2012`

§§ `9 -- Cats exempt from registration (s. 5(2)(c) and 9(2)(b))`

-- reg 9(2): "a cat that is in the custody of any of the following is exempt from
-- registration -- (a) Cat Welfare Society Inc., trading as "Cat Haven";
-- (b) The Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, Western
-- Australia; (c) the Department of State of the Commonwealth that is
-- administered by the Commonwealth Minister administering the Biosecurity Act
-- 2015 (Commonwealth); (d) a cat management facility; (e) veterinary premises as
-- defined in the Veterinary Practice Act 2021 section 3."
--
-- An enum, because custody is single-valued here: the regulation asks whose
-- custody the cat is in, and `nobody listed` is the ordinary case.
DECLARE Custodian IS ONE OF
    `Cat Haven`                                                          -- (a)
    `the RSPCA in Western Australia`                                     -- (b)
    `the Commonwealth department administering the Biosecurity Act 2015`  -- (c)
    `a cat management facility`                                          -- (d)
    `veterinary premises under the Veterinary Practice Act 2021 section 3` -- (e)
    `nobody listed in regulation 9(2)`

-- reg 9(3): "a cat that is in foster care is exempt from registration if --
-- (a) the cat has been placed into that foster care by either of the following
-- -- (i) Cat Welfare Society Inc., trading as "Cat Haven"; (ii) The Royal
-- Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, Western Australia; or
-- (b) the cat has been placed into that foster care by a SAFE entity, provided
-- that the cat has not been in foster care for more than a total of 12 weeks".
--
-- The proviso attaches to limb (b) only: a Cat Haven or RSPCA placement carries
-- no time limit, a SAFE placement expires at 12 weeks. That asymmetry is the
-- whole content of the paragraph, so the placer is an enum and the weeks are a
-- number.
DECLARE FosterPlacer IS ONE OF
    `Cat Haven`                          -- reg 9(3)(a)(i)
    `the RSPCA in Western Australia`     -- reg 9(3)(a)(ii)
    `a SAFE entity`                      -- reg 9(3)(b)
    `nobody listed in regulation 9(3)`

DECLARE CustodyFacts HAS
    `in the custody of`                  IS A Custodian
    `in foster care`                     IS A BOOLEAN
    `placed into that foster care by`    IS A FosterPlacer
    `total weeks the cat has been in foster care` IS A NUMBER

GIVEN `the facts` IS A CustodyFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `regulation 9(2) exempts the cat` IF
    CONSIDER `the facts`'s `in the custody of`
    WHEN `nobody listed in regulation 9(2)` THEN FALSE
    OTHERWISE TRUE

GIVEN `the facts` IS A CustodyFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `regulation 9(3) exempts the cat` IF
        "a cat that is in foster care" ... `the facts`'s `in foster care`
    AND CONSIDER `the facts`'s `placed into that foster care by`
        WHEN `Cat Haven` THEN TRUE
        WHEN `the RSPCA in Western Australia` THEN TRUE
        WHEN `a SAFE entity` THEN
            "provided that the cat has not been in foster care for more than a total of 12 weeks"
                ... `the facts`'s `total weeks the cat has been in foster care` AT MOST 12
        OTHERWISE FALSE

-- What s 5(2)(c) and s 9(2)(b) of the Act read as `of a class prescribed as
-- exempt from registration`.
GIVEN `the facts` IS A CustodyFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the cat is of a class prescribed as exempt from registration` IF
        `regulation 9(2) exempts the cat` `the facts`
    OR  `regulation 9(3) exempts the cat` `the facts`

§§ `10 -- Cats exempt from wearing tag (s. 6(2))`

-- reg 10(1): "exhibited means exhibited for show purposes at a cat show held by
-- -- (a) Cat Owners' Association of Western Australia Incorporated; or (b) the
-- Feline Control Council of Western Australia (Inc); or (c) Australian National
-- Cats Incorporated; or (d) Cats United WA Incorporated; or (e) a body that is
-- affiliated with an organisation mentioned in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d)."
--
-- reg 10(2): "The owner of a cat that is being exhibited is exempt from the
-- requirement to ensure the cat wears its registration tag in a public place in
-- section 6(1) of the Act."
DECLARE ShowHost IS ONE OF
    `the Cat Owners' Association of Western Australia Incorporated`   -- (a)
    `the Feline Control Council of Western Australia (Inc)`           -- (b)
    `Australian National Cats Incorporated`                           -- (c)
    `Cats United WA Incorporated`                                     -- (d)
    `a body affiliated with one of those organisations`               -- (e)
    `a host not listed in regulation 10(1)`

DECLARE ShowFacts HAS
    `exhibited for show purposes at a cat show` IS A BOOLEAN
    `the show was held by`                      IS A ShowHost

-- What s 6(2) of the Act reads as `of a class prescribed as exempt from wearing
-- a tag in a public place`. Note that the regulation exempts THE OWNER of a cat
-- being exhibited, while s 6(2) speaks of a CLASS OF CATS prescribed as exempt:
-- the regulation answers a question the Act did not quite ask. Recorded as a
-- finding; encoded as the regulation reads, since it is the regulation that
-- creates the exemption.
GIVEN `the facts` IS A ShowFacts
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the cat is of a class prescribed as exempt from wearing a tag in a public place` IF
        "a cat that is being exhibited" ... `the facts`'s `exhibited for show purposes at a cat show`
    AND CONSIDER `the facts`'s `the show was held by`
        WHEN `a host not listed in regulation 10(1)` THEN FALSE
        OTHERWISE TRUE

§§ `12 -- Period of registration (s. 9(7))`

-- reg 12(1): "Registration of a cat may be for -- (a) either one year or 3
-- years; or (b) for the life of the cat."
DECLARE RegistrationPeriod IS ONE OF
    `one year`
    `3 years`
    `the life of the cat`

-- reg 12(2)(a): registration "has effect from the period specified in the
-- registration certificate until -- (i) in the case of registration for one
-- year -- the next 31 October, unless cancelled sooner; or (ii) in the case of
-- registration for 3 years -- 31 October in the final year of that period,
-- unless cancelled sooner; or (iii) in the case of registration for the life of
-- the cat -- the death of the cat, unless cancelled sooner".
--
-- So every fixed-term registration expires on 31 October, whatever month it was
-- granted in. A one-year registration granted in September runs about six weeks.
GIVEN `the period` IS A RegistrationPeriod
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the registration expires on a 31 October` IF
    CONSIDER `the period`
    WHEN `one year` THEN TRUE
    WHEN `3 years` THEN TRUE
    WHEN `the life of the cat` THEN FALSE

-- reg 12(2)(b): registration "may be renewed to take effect as from 1 November
-- in any year, within the preceding period of 21 days."
--
-- INTERPRETIVE FORK, recorded in registers/fork-register.json as FORK-1. "the
-- preceding period of 21 days" before 1 November is either 11-31 October (21
-- days counted back inclusive of 31 October) or 12-31 October (21 clear days
-- before 1 November). The reading taken is 11-31 October; the other is live.
-- Both are asserted in cat-cases.l4 so that a change of reading is visible.
GIVEN `the date of the renewal application` IS A DATE
GIVETH A BOOLEAN
DECIDE `the renewal is within the period allowed by regulation 12(2)(b)` IF
        "in October" ... DATE_MONTH `the date of the renewal application` EQUALS 10
    AND "within the preceding period of 21 days"
            ... DATE_DAY `the date of the renewal application` AT LEAST 11
